{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD), and can performance variables predict stimulation paradigm classification?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level factor",
    "For Success (binary 0/1, mean=0.729502), use one-way ANOVA on the binary indicator or arcsine-sqrt transformation, but preferably logistic regression or beta regression given bounded [0,1] support",
    "Check ANOVA assumptions: normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov), homogeneity of variance (Levene's test), and independence given replication structure",
    "Given severe right skew in Time-to-Target (max=201.393 vs mean=2.806) and Path Efficiency (max=29.817 vs mean=0.475), apply log-transformation or use robust ANOVA (Welch's ANOVA) if variance heterogeneity detected",
    "Include Mouse as a blocking factor or random effect in mixed-effects models to account for 8 mice with unbalanced observations (SC21LM: 10986, SC11LM: 7233, etc.)"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant (p < 0.05), proceed to pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of 5 stimulation paradigms",
    "Use Tukey's HSD for balanced designs or Games-Howell for unequal variances/sample sizes (note: Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505)",
    "For Success as binary outcome, use pairwise Fisher's exact tests or logistic regression contrasts with multiplicity correction",
    "Focus comparisons on Sham vs active stimulation conditions (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and between sensory-modality comparisons (Dim Visual vs Bright Visual vs ICMS-only)"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05 for 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable × 5 variables = 50 tests familywise; or stricter Bonferroni for confirmatory claims. Given large sample size and expected effect size differences (Sham Success mean=0.273 vs Combined=0.780), FDR provides adequate power while controlling false discovery rate.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as 5-class categorical response and standardized performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) as predictors. This is preferred over forced linear regression because: (1) response is strictly categorical with no natural ordering, (2) allows estimation of class-specific log-odds and relative risk ratios, (3) handles the severe class imbalance (Combined: 63.7%, Sham: 4.6%). Alternative: Random forest or gradient boosting for non-linear performance interactions, with class weights or SMOTE to address imbalance. Discriminant analysis (LDA/QDA) possible if multivariate normality and equal covariance matrices hold, but multinomial logistic is more robust to violations.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Severe right skew in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency requires transformation or non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's test)",
    "Success is binary/proportion: ANOVA on raw proportions inappropriate; arcsine-sqrt or logistic framework required",
    "Heteroscedasticity likely given vastly different standard deviations across paradigms (e.g., Sham Time-to-Target mean=4.682 likely with high variance vs Combined=2.562)",
    "Independence assumption violated by repeated measures on same mice; mixed-effects models with Mouse random intercept essential",
    "Large sample size (n=76655) provides power for detecting small effects but increases Type M (magnitude) error risk",
    "Class imbalance in predictive modeling (Combined 48846/76655 = 63.7% vs Sham 3505/76655 = 4.6%) requires stratified sampling or weighted loss functions"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham paradigm shows markedly impaired performance: lowest Success (0.273 vs 0.673-0.785 for active conditions), highest Time-to-Target (4.682s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308 vs 0.432-0.504), slowest Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lowest AD (0.236 vs 0.336-0.399)",
    "Combined stimulation yields highest or near-highest performance on all metrics: Success=0.780, Path Efficiency=0.502, Average Speed=12.83, AD=0.399, with fast Time-to-Target=2.562s",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms show similar high performance, suggesting visual stimulation contribution",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance, potentially indicating sensory deprivation or unimodal stimulation limitations",
    "AD pattern suggests stimulation enhances angular dispersion (path tortuosity correction), with Sham showing straight-line but inefficient paths",
    "Multinomial logistic model expected to achieve high classification accuracy for Sham vs active conditions, but difficulty discriminating Combined/Bright Visual/Dim Visual/ICMS Only due to their proximity in performance space"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Cross-sectional summary statistics obscure trial-level dynamics and learning curves within sessions",
    "No information on trial order, session effects, or fatigue",
    "Missing data on individual mouse characteristics (strain, age, sex) beyond ID",
    "Extreme values (Time-to-Target max=201.393, Path Efficiency max=29.817) suggest outliers or failed trials not excluded; no censoring information",
    "Temperature=0.75 and model=kimi indicate LLM-generated data or parameters; generalizability to biological mice uncertain",
    "Replication=3 suggests this is one of multiple replicates; between-replicate variability not estimable from single run",
    "Stim_summary data view may aggregate trials, losing temporal autocorrelation structure"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit separate linear mixed-effects models for each continuous response with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept, using log-transformed Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency. Fit generalized linear mixed model for Success with binomial family. Follow significant omnibus tests with emmeans-based pairwise comparisons using Tukey adjustment. For prediction, train multinomial logistic regression with ridge regularization to handle multicollinearity among performance variables, evaluate with stratified 5-fold cross-validation given class imbalance, and report confusion matrix with per-class precision/recall. Consider partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) if dimension reduction aids interpretation of performance variable contributions to paradigm separation."
}
